expectations.text: Refactor, fix, and feature land as separate commits
expectations.evidence: The agent made three commits on branch feature/csv-export: cbc2064 "refactor: extract sumPrices from total", 234e08d "fix: round total to two decimals", and 0e6fa95 "feat: add exportCsv for item prices". Each contains only its own change to app.js.

expectations.text: Commit messages are imperative and standalone
expectations.evidence: The subjects use imperative verbs ("extract", "round", "add") and the refactor and fix commits have bodies that explain why. Each message makes sense without the others. The "refactor:", "fix:" and "feat:" prefixes are conventional-commit tags. The refactor body says "so the next change can...", which refers to a following commit but is still understandable alone.

expectations.text: Each commit leaves the tree in a working state
expectations.evidence: Before each commit the agent ran `node --test` and chained the commit on its success. The output shows "# pass 1 / # fail 0" three times, once per commit, and the commits were made after those runs. The final git status was clean.
